name: Passpack
summary: Team password manager for small businesses and MSPs. Store, share and organize credentials with zero-knowledge encryption, role-based access, MFA, device registration, full audit trails and shared team vaults, at a low per-user price. An iOS app arrived in August 2026; Android is announced but not yet out.
best_for: teams under twenty people who want zero-knowledge encryption and shared vaults at about $1.67 a seat a month, and can live with a first-generation mobile app and a plainer interface
skip_if: your team runs on Android phones or you need a settled mobile app and hand-holding support: there was still no Android app and no Play Store listing on 6 September 2026, 1Password is more polished and Bitwarden's free tier is more generous
honest_knock:
The honest trade-off is maturity, not security. The interface is plain, the mobile side is very new, and some users report slow support and billing hiccups. You are trading polish and a settled mobile experience for price and solid zero-knowledge encryption.

Android is the concrete form of that trade. The iOS app arrived on 10 August 2026; twenty-seven days later, on 6 September 2026, there was still no Android app. Passpack's own Downloads menu offered only iOS and the browser extension, and a Google Play search for 'passpack' that day returned thirteen apps, all of them rival password managers and none of them this one. If your team is on Android, plan as though the app does not exist, because it does not.

Their own pages lag their announcements, too, though less than they did. Passpack told partners on 2 September 2026 that TOTP now works on every plan, and on 3 September the word appeared on neither the plans nor the key-features page; by 6 September the plans comparison table lists both TOTP and 'Mobile app for iOS', in the section that carries no plan exclusions. The key-features page has not caught up: on 6 September it still listed 'Mobile & Browser Extensions' under New Features Coming Soon, four weeks after iOS shipped and with the extensions already sold on the plans page. Read the plans table rather than the newsletter, and confirm stored TOTP codes inside the 28-day trial.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 30 September 2026 on passpack.com/plans/ and passpack.com/llms.txt, which agree; unchanged since our 25 August, 2, 3 and 6 September readings) Teams is $20 per user per year, paid annually, for teams of up to 20 people. Business is $4.50 per user per month, paid annually, includes everything in Teams and has a monthly option. Enterprise is a custom quote, and both paid plans carry a 28-day free trial. The gap between those two matters more than either number: Teams works out at about $1.67 a user a month, while Business at $4.50 sits inside the $3 to $8 range the mainstream managers charge. The saving is real on Teams and largely gone above twenty people. What changed between 3 and 6 September 2026 is the feature table rather than the price: the plans page now lists TOTP and 'Mobile app for iOS' under Admin & User Functionality, the section that carries no plan exclusions, so both apply to all three plans.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Passpack on a Business trial: a made up record without any password, a multi-administrator team, sharing the record with the team, and two reports. No password was entered in this test. The test record has an empty password field, a made up username and an example web address, so no real login or credential was typed, generated or stored. The record form has the fields Recordnaam, Gebruikersnaam, E-mail, Wachtwoord (with a generator and strength meter), TOTP, Website-URL and Etiketten. The record Test: shared social media login was saved with the password left empty (Nieuw record aangemaakt) and defaults to Privé. The team Marketing (test) was created with the default member rights Kan bekijken or Kan bewerken and the team mode Privé or Multi-beheerder; Multi-beheerder was chosen (Nieuw team aangemaakt). Sharing: on the record the sharing mode must be changed first (Houd privé, Eigendom overdragen or Deel met teams met meerdere beheerders); only then the team list appears. From the Opnames tab of the team the private record could not be added. Switching on Marketing (test) in the team list opened the confirmation Instellingen voor delen updaten?, which says the record can then be managed by all administrators of the organisation, and the change was saved. This took about 6 clicks and the route was not easy to find. The Teamlidmaatschap report searches by email and shows team name, team owner and user permission; a search on the own account gave Geen resultaten gevonden, so the owner does not count as a member. The Toegang tot logboeken report lists sign in activity per login and offers a CSV download; no screenshot of it is used and its contents are not reproduced here. A departing colleague was not simulated because no second user was invited. The only app banner promotes the iPhone app; no Android app was offered inside the app. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Sharing a private record with a team needed about 6 clicks and a change of sharing mode first; adding the record from the team side did not work.

sessions.what: We tested team sharing in Passpack on a Business trial on 13 November 2026 with a made-up record that holds no password. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We typed, generated and stored no password and no real login: the record has an empty password field, an invented username and an example web address. We invited no second user, so a departing colleague was not simulated.
findings: The record form has fields for name, username, email, password (with a generator and a strength meter), TOTP, website address and tags. We saved the record with the password left empty. It defaults to private.
We created a team called 'Marketing (test)' with default member rights of view or edit, and chose the Multi-administrator mode over Private.

Sharing took about 6 clicks and the route was hard to find. On the record, the sharing mode must change first (keep private, transfer ownership, or share with multi-administrator teams). Only then does the team list appear. Adding the private record from the team's own records tab did not work.
Switching the team on opened a confirmation saying the record can then be managed by all administrators of the organisation. We confirmed and it saved.

The Team Membership report searches by email and shows team name, team owner and user permission. A search on our own account returned no results, so the owner does not count as a member there. The Log Access report lists sign-in activity per login and offers a CSV download. We did not open the file.

The account showed a Business plan with status Trial and no card was requested. The trial end date was not visible because the renewal date field was empty, so we could not confirm the '28 days' on the pricing page.

The Subscription page says the contract renews automatically with the number of licences used, currently 1. We did not open the Stripe billing portal and saw no price, tax or total. The only mobile banner promoted the iPhone app. We saw no Android app offered inside the app, and did not check whether one exists elsewhere.
